pr_title: fix: support pnpm workspace path aliasing
pr_body:
### Description

Fixes #6744 

I highly suggest reviewing each commit on it's own as the code move done in the first commit makes the cumulative diff hard to understand. I wanted to clean up this code a bit as we'll need to extend it further for supporting https://github.com/vercel/turbo/issues/7188

This adds support for the PNPM feature of [aliasing a package via path](https://pnpm.io/workspaces#referencing-workspace-packages-through-their-relative-path). 

The slightly tricky part of this is that there are many valid specifiers for the `workspace:` protocol. We currently support `workspace:1.2.3`, `workspace:*`, [`workspace:bar@*`](https://pnpm.io/workspaces#referencing-workspace-packages-through-aliases), `workspace:../path/to/package`.

### Testing Instructions

Added unit tests for the case of a dependency of the form `"foo": "workspace:../bar"` where `foo` is another workspace package.

Verified fix works with repro provided in: https://github.com/vercel/turbo/issues/6744

issue_context.title: Wrong dependent task gets run when using pnpm relative path reference (eg. `workspace:../path/to/dep`)
issue_context.body:
### Verify canary release

- [X] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Turborepo canary release.

### Link to code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/steveluscher/pnpm-alias-pathspec-repro.git

### What package manager are you using / does the bug impact?

pnpm

### What operating system are you using?

Mac

### Which canary version will you have in your reproduction?

1.11.1-canary.0

### Describe the Bug

Imagine that you:

1. Alias a package to a relative path (eg. `"luigi": "workspace:../waluigi"`)
2. Another package in your workspace has the same name as the alias (`luigi`)

…then you run some turborepo task.

```shell
pnpm i
cd packages/app/
pnpm turbo hello
```

Turborepo will run the task in the wrong workspace package; the `hello` script from `luigi/package.json` runs.


### Expected Behavior

Since the dependency `luigi` is aliased to `workspace:../waluigi`, I would expect the `hello` script from `waluigi/package.json` to run.

### To Reproduce

Follow the README in https://github.com/steveluscher/pnpm-alias-pathspec-repro.git.

### Additional context

> [!NOTE]
> If you change the dependency in `app/package.json` from `"luigi": "workspace:../waluigi"` to `"luigi": "workspace:waluigi@*"` it works as expected.

<sub>[TURBO-1899](https://linear.app/vercel/issue/TURBO-1899/wrong-dependent-task-gets-run-when-using-pnpm-relative-path-reference)</sub>
comments:
I know this isn't a fix for the underlying issue, but could you use the other `pnpm` [alias strategy](https://pnpm.io/workspaces#referencing-workspace-packages-through-aliases) to unblock yourself?
e.g. in `packages/app/package.json` change the dependency to be `"luigi": "workspace:waluigi@*"`

I mentioned that alternate strategy in a note in the original issue text, yeah. That strategy won't work for me for reasons that I shouldn't get into here. I just want to make sure that Vercel is aware of the bug in Turbo.
Ah, my bad for not reading the issue closely enough. Thanks for opening the issue and the repro.

review_comments: The code linked above appears to check for backslashes on windows. Should we do that?

Luckily in this case pnpm does not generate `workspace:..\windows-path` and expects these to be unix style.

The npa code is used a lot of places, but luckily here we don't have to worry about the "is this path a system or unix style" question.
